the AT2 receptor is present in many regions of the central nervous system and that it is involved in the control of blood pressure and the secretion of hormones.

the elucidation of the functional role of the AT2 angiotension II receptor in the brain.
the characterization of the angiotensin receptor subtypes AT1 and AT2 in the rat brain.
the localization of AT2 angio- tensin II receptor gene and receptor expression in rat brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AT2 receptor gene and receptor protein are co-expressed in several areas of the brain, but in others only the receptor protein is present.
AT2 receptors are expressed in brain regions where the receptor protein is also found, and that AT2 receptors may also be expressed in brain regions that do not contain the receptor protein.

AT2 receptor expression and gene expression in the brain do not always correspond, and that the localization of AT2 receptor gene transcription is not a reliable indicator of the localization of AT1 receptor expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AT2 receptor is a novel and important receptor system in the brain.
AT2 receptor mRNA is expressed in the brain in areas where AT2 receptors are present and in areas where AT1 receptors are expressed.
the AT2 receptor mRNA is found in the brain regions where the receptor protein is also expressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AT2 receptor gene is highly expressed in the thalamus and the cerebellum.
AT2 angiotension receptors are found in the brain, and that they are involved in the regulation of blood pressure.
the AT2 receptor has a role in the brain, and that it is a target for drugs that are being developed.
